references.text: Elijah gave the resurrected boy back to his mother with the words "See, your son lives" – a direct parallel to Jesus' act of giving the dead young man back to his mother in Nain.
Elisha raised the Shunammite woman's son from the dead and returned him to her mother, which is a clear parallel to Jesus raising the widow's son in Nain.
Peter raises Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead and returns her to the believers, a parallel to Jesus' act of giving the resurrected one back to their loved ones.
The crowd's reaction to the resurrection was to praise God and say that a great prophet had risen among them – this is the immediate context and response to the raising of the dead.
Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead, and the dead man came out – a parallel to how the dead person in Nain sat up and began to speak.
Jesus raises Jairus' daughter from the dead, and her spirit returned – another resurrection performed by Jesus with parallels to the event in Nain.
Elijah prayed to the Lord and the child's soul returned so that he lived again – an Old Testament parallel where a prophet raises a dead person to life.
Paul raises the young man Eutychus, who had fallen from the third story and was dead, and returns him alive to the church.
